thread:
Erin K: heads-up — CI perf alert after merge of the hybrid-quant shim (merge 3342). small-batch p95 up ~30%, p99 up ~45% on our lm-small traces. not seeing accuracy regressions yet but latency regression is real. can we pause the canary? :eyes:
Mark L: link to the CI job? which benchmark is spiking?
Erin K: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/90712 — compare 'decode_small' baseline vs post-merge. attached perf summary: total token-ms increased, and tail shows long dequant stalls.
perf-bot: ALERT: perf-ci/job/90712 exceeded threshold (p95 latency +32%). Regression detected by perf-diff.
Sasha P: I grabbed a flamegraph from the canary run. looks like we added an extra memcpy + format-conversion in the shim on the hotpath. excerpt:
```
# flamegraph stack (top samples)
dequant_shim::convert_format
  memcpy
  cpu_convert_loop
runtime::kv_cache_access
  batch_scheduler::coalesce_wait
```
Erin K: that matches my local sampling. the shim was meant to be a low-cost adapter for mixed-int8/fp8 kernels but ended up materializing a different layout per-request.
Juan R: I started a git-bisect on the perf CI seed. earliest bad commit points to 9c3b7f1 (PR 3342) — the change was "move dequant from kernel into shim for unified path". when I force the old kernel-local dequant we go back to baseline.
Simon T: Interesting — when dequant lived in kernel we could fuse it with unpack and avoid a memcopy. shim approach breaks that fusion and also increases KV cache pressure (extra allocations).
Mark L: any repro script? can we run a microbenchmark with batch sizes [1,2,4] and kv-hits/misses to see interaction?
Juan R: repro script: `scripts/perf/run_decode_suite.sh --model lm-small --batches 1,2,4 --kv-locality low` — run with flamegraph and `--record-kvcache`. outputs show ~2x increase in kvcache eviction rate for batch=1 after shim.
Sasha P: attaching perf diff snapshot (sha: perf/1729). also tried pinning to single-threaded CPU and still see the memcpy cost dominating at short sequences.
Erin K: proposal: revert PR 3342 for canary and we iterate to push conversion back into kernel (or expose a fused path). open to alternatives: make the shim do buffer-pool reuse + in-place conversion to avoid allocs.
Mark L: +1 revert for immediate mitigation. please file postmortem and a follow-up PR to present microbench results and a fused path plan.
deploy-bot: Deploy hold set on canary group "quant-canary" by Mark L.
Erin K: I'll open the revert PR now and add the perf artifacts to the issue. pinging @Sasha P and @Juan R for follow-up on kernel-fusion feasibility.
Sasha P: quick note — if we do in-place convert we need to update kernel kernels to accept that layout; might be a perf win but increases kernel complexity. I'll prototype a variant.
Juan R: For the bisect logs: `git bisect log` attached to thread. suspected commit: 9c3b7f1 -> changes to shim_alloc & convert_format.
Simon T: Also consider scheduler tweak as a short-term workaround: raise the small-batch coalescing timeout by 2ms to allow grouping that hides the shim overhead (tradeoff on latency tail though).
Erin K: Decision: revert PR 3342 on main (Mark L approved), hold canary, bisect artifacts + flamegraphs archived. action items: Erin open revert, Sasha prototype fused kernel, Juan produce deterministic kvcache microbench.
Mark L: Thanks all. good catch on the fusion loss. :thumbsup:
Erin K: filing the issue and PR now — I'll paste links once created.
Mark L: keep this thread updated with PR numbers and perf diffs.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for eng-runtime perf regression; contains root and replies in chronological order. Messages are short and Slack-like, include code snippets and bot messages.
